title: 4 best AI motion control tools for character animation
summary: Compare AI motion control tools for character animation and performance transfer. Check inputs, scene preservation, free limits and cost per usable clip.
body_markdown:
For a quick browser workflow that animates a character image from a reference performance, start with **Magic Hour Character Animate** . Choose **Runway Act-Two** when facial performance and speech are central, **Viggle** for character-motion remixes, or **ImagineArt** when you specifically want its hosted Kling motion-control workflow.


The deciding question is what must survive the transformation: the character's appearance, the source performance, or the original scene. “Motion control” can describe different products, and a good still frame does not prove that a moving result is usable.

Product documentation and access information checked September 11, 2026. This is a workflow-based shortlist, not a scored output benchmark. Magic Hour publishes this guide; the alternatives are included for their different documented capabilities.


## 1. Magic Hour: a direct character-animation workflow


[Character Animate](https://magichour.ai/products/motion-control) takes a character still and a driving video. It is a sensible starting point when you have already chosen how the character and scene should look and want to apply a performance to that image.


The important limitation is scene preservation. Magic Hour's product instructions say the image supplies the background. If you need to keep the original video's surroundings while changing its subject, use[Character Replace](https://magichour.ai/products/character-replace) instead. That decision avoids spending credits on the wrong kind of transformation.


Prepare a clearly visible character and a reference with similar framing. Generate a short section first, then inspect the full movement before committing to a longer clip.


## 2. Runway Act-Two: facial performance and speech


[Runway's Act-Two documentation](https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/42311337895827-Performance-Capture-with-Act-Two) describes transferring a driving performance to a character image or video, including speech and expressions. This makes it relevant when the performance is an actor delivering a line, rather than simply a character following a dance.


The input choice matters: body and hand gesture control is available with a character image; a character video retains that video's body motion. Do not treat these as interchangeable modes. Check the chosen input, supported duration and current credit quote before planning a sequence.


## 3. Viggle: character-motion remixes


[Viggle](https://viggle.ai/) offers tools for adding motion to a character and replacing characters in clips. Consider it for a short character remix where the recognizable movement is the core of the idea.


Its[pricing page](https://viggle.ai/pricing) lists five free videos per day, a one-minute maximum upload on Free, and watermark removal on paid plans. A listed upload allowance is not a promise that every model or operation produces that full duration. Read the selected operation's quote.


Viggle also offers PINOC for motion capture. Choose that separate route only if you need its 3D workflow; a finished character video and reusable 3D motion data are different deliverables.


## 4. ImagineArt: a hosted Kling motion-control option


[ImagineArt's motion-control page](https://www.imagine.art/apps/motion-control) describes a Kling 3.0 workflow using a character image and a motion reference or preset. It is an option when you want motion transfer within ImagineArt's wider creative workspace.


ImagineArt is the platform; Kling is the model named for this workflow. A Kling subscription elsewhere does not establish shared access or credits. Compare the actual model, duration, resolution and generation quote inside the platform you intend to use.


## Motion transfer, camera control or character replacement?


These are different starting points:


- **Copy a performance onto a still character:** use an image-plus-motion-reference workflow from this guide.
- **Invent a camera move around a product photo:** start with[image-to-video](https://magichour.ai/products/image-to-video) and the selected model's camera or prompting controls.
- **Keep a filmed scene but replace its subject:** evaluate character replacement and check what happens to the background.
- **Match a filmed face to new speech:** use[lip sync](https://magichour.ai/products/lip-sync) with the video and desired audio.


For broader generation choices, see the[AI video generator comparison](https://magichour.ai/blog/best-ai-video-generators) . For a still-image workflow without a driving performance, use the[image-to-video guide](https://magichour.ai/blog/best-image-to-video-generators) .


## A five-second brief that makes comparisons useful


Use the same character image and permitted reference clip in each compatible tool. A useful starter performance is: face forward, raise one hand, turn slightly, lower the hand, return to the starting pose. Keep the character's hands and feet inside the frame if the shot needs them.


Before generating, write down five acceptance checks:


1. The face remains recognizable through the turn.
2. The hand stays attached and returns to the expected position.
3. Clothing and distinctive marks remain stable.
4. The important gesture happens at the intended moment.
5. The background behaves as the chosen workflow promises.


Save the full output, input files, model name, settings, generation quote and whether you accepted the clip. This is a suggested evaluation brief, not a test we claim to have run. A longer or more acrobatic performance needs a separate evaluation.


## What does a usable motion-control clip cost?


Compare the cost of **accepted output** , including unsuccessful attempts. Subscription prices alone hide differences in model cost and retry rate.


For example, suppose a five-second attempt costs 20 credits and three attempts produce one acceptable clip. That clip used 60 credits, or 12 credits per accepted second. These are illustrative numbers, not any provider's tariff. Convert them using your actual purchased credit cost, and include required plan fees when comparing total spend.


For recurring work, also consider review time. A cheap generation that needs extensive masking or repair may cost more to finish than a more expensive result that already satisfies the brief.

These changes make the input easier to interpret; they cannot guarantee an artifact-free result. Review at normal speed and pause around turns, crossings and fast movements.


## Frequently asked questions


### What is AI motion control?


In character animation, AI motion control uses a reference performance to guide how a different character moves. The character's appearance and the motion can come from separate inputs. Some tools use the same phrase for camera direction, so check the required inputs before choosing one.


### Does motion control also generate audio?


Not necessarily. Performance transfer, dialogue generation and adding a soundtrack are separate capabilities. Check the selected mode's documentation and listen to the downloaded file before assuming speech or music is included.


### Can I use motion control for a commercial character?


Use a character and performance you have permission to use, and check the selected service's terms for the intended distribution. Then review identity, costume and product details through the entire output. A paid plan does not establish rights to someone else's character or performance.


### What should I try first?


If you have a character still and a short reference performance,[try Character Animate](https://magichour.ai/products/motion-control) with a five-second sample. Confirm that its scene behavior matches your brief, then evaluate the complete clip before extending the job.
